extracted.intended_audience: physician-scientists (applicants) and institutional officials preparing CAMS proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions, eligibility rules, and application/award requirements for Burroughs Wellcome Fund Career Awards for Medical Scientists (CAMS), a five-year career award for physician-scientists bridging advanced training and early faculty service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose and target candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Career Awards for Medical Scientists (CAMS) provides $700,000 awards over five years for physician-scientists committed to an academic career to bridge advanced postdoctoral/fellowship training and the early years of faculty service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program is highly competitive and intended to support physician-scientists transitioning to faculty roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field scope of research
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is only for individuals in basic biomedical, disease-oriented, or translational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields such as health services research and policy are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree and candidate type eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be physician-scientists; holders of Ph.D.-only, Pharm.D., or Pharm.D./Ph.D. degrees are not eligible for CAMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your background is in physical/mathematical/computational sciences or engineering addressing biological questions, consider other BWF programs (e.g., Career Awards at the Scientific Interface).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have at least one first-author publication to be competitive and eligible to apply for this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared first authorship counts. Accepted or in-press manuscripts qualify; bioRxiv pre-prints count. Publications solely as non-first author do not meet this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional affiliation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Public or private non-profit organizations in the United States and Canada, including degree-granting academic institutions, research institutes, and teaching hospitals affiliated with degree-granting institutions, are eligible to receive BWF support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications from other nonprofit organizations may be considered subject to program officer approval. Clinical degrees awarded outside the US/Canada are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be approved by an official at the institution responsible for sponsored programs (generally grants & contracts, office of research, or sponsored programs office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although self-nomination is allowed, institutional sign-off is required prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected research effort expectation (75% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The expectation for CAMS is that 75% of the applicant's time will be devoted to research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants need not currently have 75% protected time at submission, but must demonstrate that such time can be negotiated if CAMS is awarded (e.g., letters of support or offer letter). Surgeons are expected to meet the same 75% expectation. Provide documentation if protected time is to be negotiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility re: existing awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with NIH K08, K12, K21, or K23 awards are eligible; applicants with NIH K99/R00 or Early Independence awards (e.g., DP5) are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees cannot receive funding simultaneously from both a K99 or DP5 and a CAMS award. Award recipients may not hold concurrent BWF awards or NIH K99/R00, NIH DP5, or similar Early Independence awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current faculty appointment rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If you currently hold or have accepted, verbally or in writing, a tenure-track faculty appointment, you are not eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-tenure track instructor/clinical lecturer/assistant professor appointments are acceptable if all other eligibility criteria are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing institutions after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not change your training environment (mentor and institution) after submitting the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitations to finalists and interview eligibility are based on information submitted. If you move to a new institution after submitting the proposal, you will not be eligible to interview even if invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission method and deadline firmness
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be submitted electronically via Proposal Central by the application deadline. The deadline is firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper applications will not be accepted. You can save and return to an application in Proposal Central prior to the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single application and no changes after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit only one application and, once submitted, you cannot change your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure completeness before final submission; multiple applications are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required forms: Signature Page and Institutional Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Signature Page Form (with applicant signature) and the Institutional Certification Form signed by an authorized official are required; an application is not complete without them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional Certification certifies non-profit degree-granting status and applicant eligibility at submission. Emailed/mailed/faxed signature or certification forms will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support letters: mentor and recommendation letters policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one mentor letter of recommendation may be submitted and it should be from the primary postdoctoral mentor or faculty sponsor. Applicants commonly also include additional recommendation letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a co-mentor/secondary mentor, the primary and secondary mentor may co-write and sign one mentor letter, or the secondary mentor may instead write one of your additional recommendation letters. All support letters must be uploaded and attached to your application in Proposal Central by the deadline; emailed/mailed/faxed letters will not be accepted. Letters should be addressed to the CAMS Advisory Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials allowed and appendices prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not include materials beyond those requested by the application instructions; including additional materials may disqualify you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only requested documents and forms should be uploaded. If a bibliography or glossaries are included, they do not count toward the page limit (see research plan page limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research plan page limit and what counts
rubrics_metrics.description: The research plan has a six-page maximum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures, tables, graphs, diagrams, and pictures included in the research plan count toward the six-page limit. Bibliography and glossaries of technical abbreviations/terms do NOT count toward the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font, spacing, and margin requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard 11- or 12-point type for text; figures/legends/tables must be no smaller than 9-10 point. Text must be single-spaced with one inch or larger margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The font size requirement is strictly enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget requirement and salary/fringe limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A tentative budget associated with your project plan must be included, and there are specified limits for salary and fringe amounts during the award phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using the postdoctoral portion (up to two years): maximum of $90,000 for salary+fringe in year one and $95,000 in year two. During the faculty portion: a maximum of $59,500 may be used annually toward the named investigator's salary and fringe combined. Caregiver expenses up to $5,000/year may be budgeted separately and can be used during any portion of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reporting cadence and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must update award spending in the Proposal Central budget summary and submit financial reports twice each year with up-to-date spending info from the prior six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial reports are due biannually on February 1 and August 1. Failure to submit required financial updates will result in payments being withheld and may lead to termination for repeated misses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress report cadence and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must submit an annual progress report including a written report on progress of original or approved updated research aims, an updated biographical sketch, a letter of support, and any recent publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress reports are due annually on November 1 and must be submitted through Proposal Central. Failure to submit timely progress reports inconveniences reviewers and may lead to payment withholding or termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report and deliverable submission portal
rubrics_metrics.description: All progress and financial reporting materials and required deliverables must be submitted through Proposal Central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required deliverables are listed on the Proposal Central home page after logging in. Contact program staff (e.g., Lama Haidar) with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No appendices or extra materials policy (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include additional materials beyond those requested; inclusion of extra materials may disqualify your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants sometimes attempt to add appendices; this is explicitly disallowed and may result in disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer letters / startup package review for non-tenure track appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: BWF reviews non-tenure track offers on a case-by-case basis; to be considered for eligibility, submit your full offer letter including research startup details to the CAMS team no later than two weeks prior to the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may redact salary or confidential portions. Letters will be kept confidential and used only to review eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award portability and transfer conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is portable and most awardees will change institutions to begin a faculty appointment; transfers are not guaranteed and require BWF approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receiving institution must demonstrate commitment by offering a tenure-track or equivalent faculty appointment and significant start-up funds. Transfers during the faculty portion are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interruptions and no-cost extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees may interrupt the award for family commitments with a no-cost extension of up to two years during the award term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact BWF staff to arrange approved interruptions/extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent funding policy (recipient obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients may obtain funds from other sources for research in the same or similar areas so long as there is no conflict with meeting the terms of BWF’s award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may not hold concurrent BWF awards or NIH K99/R00, NIH DP5, or similar Early Independence awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support contact and program staff guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are responsible for reading published guidelines and FAQs to determine eligibility; if questions remain, contact the CAMS team (cams@bwfund.org).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BWF will prioritize questions not already addressed in published guidelines. Do not ask for exceptions to clearly stated rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition rate expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on prior competitions, estimated award rate is approximately 12 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no guarantee—the actual number of proposals varies by cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters address and submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of recommendation must be addressed to the CAMS Advisory Committee and uploaded/attached to the application in Proposal Central; outside submissions (email/mail/fax) will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All support letters must be received electronically by the application deadline to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on co-investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: The CAMS grant program does not allow co-investigators on a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan the project and budget accordingly; additional mentors may contribute via letters but not as co-investigators.
